metadata.title: Pass 3 reduced transient coupling: quasi-static non-Euclidean valve energy -> suture crack propagation (Freund dynamic fracture) -> elastic-catapult seed ejection for Bauhinia variegata
metadata.remediation_item: Couple the quasi-static non-Euclidean shell energy minimizer to transient elastodynamic fracture propagation along the pod suture line to model ballistic seed ejection velocities.
metadata.honesty_note: This is a REDUCED 1-D model, not a 3-D elastodynamic FEM. The valve energy landscape is the Pass 2 L-BFGS-B reduced Foppl-von Karman functional; the suture crack is a 1-D Freund equation of motion; seed launch speed is an energy-partition (elastic catapult) estimate. Every constant below carries a `provenance` flag: `source` = taken from a cited paper, `derived` = computed from sourced quantities, `model` = unsourced modelling choice that the Pass 3 audit should treat as a free parameter.

governing_equations.bending_energy_prefactor: w_B = B_eff * E_bend(H, D, phi),  B_eff = Y h^3 / (12 (1 + nu))  [J/m^2 per (1/m^2)]  (Efrati et al. 2009 JMPS Eq. for the incompatible plate bending content with b_0 = diag(kappa_0, -kappa_0): A^{ijkl}(b-b_0)_{ij}(b-b_0)_{kl} = (Y/(1-nu^2)) [nu Tr(M)^2 + (1-nu) Tr(M^2)] with Tr(M) = 2H, Tr(M^2) = 2(H^2 + D^2 - 2 D kappa_0 cos 2phi + kappa_0^2))
governing_equations.released_energy_density: Delta_e(kappa_0, w_tilde) = B_eff * [E_bend(0, 0) - E(H*, D*, phi*)] = B_eff * [kappa_0^2 - e_final]  (closed flat pod -> relaxed free valve; e_final from the quasi-static minimizer)
governing_equations.suture_energy_release_rate: G = Delta_e * W / h_suture  (energy released per unit suture crack advance per valve, divided by created crack area h_suture * da; two valves share two sutures)
governing_equations.hygroscopic_drying_trajectory: kappa_0(t) = kappa_0,final * (1 - exp(-t / tau_dry)),  w_tilde(t) = W sqrt(kappa_0(t) / h)
governing_equations.crack_initiation: t_c solves G(kappa_0(t_c)) = Gamma_c(a_0)  (Griffith criterion at the stylar-tip flaw a_0)
governing_equations.freund_crack_equation_of_motion: da/dt = c_R * max(0, 1 - Gamma_c(a) / G),  c_R ~= 0.93 c_s,  c_s = sqrt(Y / (2 (1 + nu) rho))  (Freund 1990 Ch. 7 mode-I approximation G_dyn(v) ~= (1 - v/c_R) G_static)
governing_equations.suture_toughness_heterogeneity: Gamma_c(a) = Gamma_c,mean * max(0.05, 1 + cv_Gamma * xi(a)),  xi = unit-variance Gaussian-smoothed noise (seeded)
governing_equations.crack_arrest: crack arrests at a* where Gamma_c(a*) >= G; opening fraction f_open = a* / L
governing_equations.elastic_catapult_seed_speed: v_seed = sqrt(2 eta Delta_U_seg / m_eff),  Delta_U_seg = Delta_e * W * l_seg,  m_eff = m_seg/3 + m_seed,  m_seg = rho h W l_seg  (Vogel 2005 J. Biosci. elastic-catapult energy budget; cantilever-tip effective mass m/3)
governing_equations.valve_coil_time: t_coil = (pi / 2) / omega_1,  omega_1 = 3.516 sqrt(B / (rho h)) / l_seg^2,  B = Y h^3 / (12 (1 - nu^2))  (first cantilever flexural mode, quarter period)
governing_equations.seed_ejection_time: t_eject,i = t_c + a_i / v_crack + t_coil  for seed i at suture position a_i (only if a_i <= a*)
governing_equations.ballistic_range: m dv/dt = m g - (1/2) rho_air C_d A |v| v,  launched at 45 deg from height z_0 (RK4), compared with the drag-free bound v^2 sin(2 alpha) / g

Y_modulus_Pa.note: Y_modulus_MPa = 420 in chiral_seed_pod_opening_reference.json default_parameters (Armon et al. 2011 SOM order of magnitude for dry sclerenchyma)

rho_valve_kg_m3.note: dry lignified sclerenchyma tissue density; typical 600-1000 kg/m^3; unsourced choice

h_suture_m.note: suture cracks through the full valve thickness

Gamma_c_mean_J_m2.note: suture fracture toughness; chosen inside the 10^2-10^3 J/m^2 range typical of plant tissue; NOT measured for Bauhinia. Swept in evaluate_suture_toughness_sweep()

cv_Gamma.note: coefficient of variation of the heterogeneous suture toughness field

a0_flaw_m.note: initial flaw at the stylar tip where dehiscence starts

tau_dry_h.note: first-order desiccation time constant on the tree

n_seeds.note: seeds per pod, evenly spaced along the suture; Bauhinia variegata pods carry ~5-15 seeds

m_seed_kg.note: flat ~1 cm Bauhinia variegata seed, 0.3-0.6 g; unsourced

r_seed_m.note: equivalent disc radius for drag area

eta_catapult.note: fraction of released elastic energy converted to kinetic energy of valve segment + seed (Vogel 2005 reports <~0.5 for biological catapults)

launch_height_m.note: pod height on an orchid tree

benchmarks.source: Hofhuis H, Moulton D, Lessinnes T, et al. (2016) Morphomechanical Innovation Drives Explosive Seed Dispersal. Cell 166(1):222-233, doi 10.1016/j.cell.2016.05.002
benchmarks.note: Different taxon and a far more violent explosive mechanism; used only as an order-of-magnitude benchmark for the ballistic speed. No published Bauhinia variegata launch-speed measurement was available offline.

benchmarks.source: Swaine MD, Beer T (1977) Explosive seed dispersal in Hura crepitans L. (Euphorbiaceae). New Phytologist 78(3):695-708, doi 10.1111/j.1469-8137.1977.tb02174.x
benchmarks.note: Upper bound of plant ballistic dispersal; Bauhinia must lie far below it.

benchmarks.source: Freund LB (1990) Dynamic Fracture Mechanics. Cambridge University Press, doi 10.1017/CBO9780511546761

toughness_sweep_design.expected_qualitative: v_crack/c_R = 1 - Gamma/G decreases linearly to 0 at Gamma = G; opening fraction drops from 1 to ~0 as Gamma/G crosses 1 (heterogeneity makes the transition smooth); ejection speed is independent of Gamma (set by Delta_e) but the number of ejected seeds falls with the opening fraction
